name: service-class-labels
goal: Service cards use their owned implementation symbol rather than an unrelated first export, with multi-export fixtures enforcing catalog label identity

evidence: The 8c15da72 card label used owns.symbols[0]. Live AnalyticsOptions and AudioUploadInput cards exposed that type exports precede AnalyticsService and AudioUploadService. Prior tables used registered service names.

The standard entity fixture had one export per service, so existing class identity assertions could not detect first-export selection. Added surrounding options/result exports to every fixture service and tied the catalog acceptance review rule to this shared coverage.

Frozen test commit 43d9c18f fails the class-name assertion at all three viewports, rendering OrderStoreOptions. Record 7036472f3a25616671e05d5da316ef899efd9adff37d4d1bfaf3d8d4991f99bb and inspected before screenshots preserve the defect.

Match recorded symbols to their owned implementation filename; retain the registered service name if none matches. The shared multi-export fixture and normal card identity assertions enforce this export-order failure class during ordinary tests.

Service labels now resolve a symbol matching an owned source filename and otherwise use the registered name. Surrounding options/result exports remain in the shared fixture and standard catalog acceptance rule.

The same multi-export card matrix and 35 focused unit tests pass at 13838843, record 754737b3ca7dd98ffae7bc07595b17fe3375517c87511fc0461dfd8ec0305e65. Inspected after screenshots show OrderStore rather than OrderStoreOptions.

Clean snapshots preserve the export-order fault at 43d9c18f and repair at 13838843. The identical shared fixture and browser assertions reject the original first-export implementation at three viewports, then pass with the repair.
